A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NoOp research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original few-shot classification, cross-dataset transfer, computational-cost and ablation results, including additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including the timestep experiments moved into Section 4.9.

M1.justification: Both versions optimize dataset-specific noise and an image-specific Meta-Network offset using normalized classification logits and cross-entropy. The architecture, optimization objective and inference procedure in Section 3 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The eight principal classification datasets, ISIC-2019 comparison and ImageNet transfer experiments are retained. Moving the CIFAR-10 timestep experiments into Section 4.9 adds no dataset, task or test scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain zero-shot DC, five-noise ensembling, TiF Learner and the appendix prompt-learning baseline. The relocated timestep comparison also retains the same zero-shot and NoOp conditions.

E3.justification: The stability experiment changes its inherited-settings reference from Section 4.1 in v1 Appendix D.5 to Section 4.8 in v2 Appendix D.3. Section 4.8 specifies noise optimization without the Meta-Network, creating uncertainty about whether this reports a procedural change or an erroneous cross-reference. Other explicit experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Component, architecture, initialization-stability, noise-role and frequency analyses are retained. v1 Appendices D.2–D.3 and Figure 8 become v2 Section 4.9 and Figure 7; their timestep ablation and ensemble evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: v1 Appendices D.2 and D.3 explicitly state that timestep results are averaged over three random seeds; the merged v2 Section 4.9 omits those statements. Three-seed reporting elsewhere remains. This is reduced experiment-specific disclosure, not evidence that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and the matched plots retain their numerical results and trends. For example, timestep-ensemble accuracy remains 78.2% for NoOp versus 72.8% for zero-shot DC, and Table 2 retains target averages of 37.65% versus 34.79%.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(15), the diffusion-classifier formulation and the Fourier definitions in Appendices A–B are retained. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims about noise instability, frequency and spatial matching, effective few-shot learning and complementarity with prompt optimization. The shortened future-work passage does not alter the claimed contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of category-related signal destruction, transferability, component complementarity and optimized-noise probability remain. Appendix F retains the limitation that inference requires a separate denoising evaluation for each candidate category.

D1.justification: The changed stability-experiment settings pointer introduces ambiguity into reproduction instructions. Otherwise, Appendix E retains the network details, scheduler, batch size, hardware and timing information, and the code-access statement is unchanged.

R1.justification: A new introductory paragraph in Appendix A adds four references covering conditional control, watermarking against image editing, image composition and concept erasure. The existing positioning relative to diffusion classifiers and noise-optimization research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 merges two appendix subsections into Section 4.9, shortens future-work discussion, adds acknowledgements and corresponding-author information, and switches to numbered citations. Most scientific prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Title, heading and header styling change, and figures and tables are repositioned. Most notably, v1 appendix Figure 8 becomes main-text Figure 7, while the additional few-shot plot becomes Figure 8. The graphics, plotted data, axes and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Moving existing timestep evidence into Section 4.9 improves visibility, but v2 drops its explicit three-seed averaging disclosures and introduces an ambiguous settings reference for the stability experiment. These changes slightly weaken reporting and reproducibility clarity. The method, empirical findings and substantive limitations remain intact, so the decline is limited.
